topic: The stethoscope was invented in France: René Théophile Hyacinthe Laennec, Necker Hospital, Paris, 1816 — a rolled paper cylinder used to hear a young woman's heart; named from Greek stethos (chest) + skopein (to look/examine); published in 'De l'auscultation médiate' (1819); Laennec died of tuberculosis in 1826 aged 45.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: The stethoscope was a British or German invention like much of 19th-century medical kit.
myths.reality: Laennec, a French physician, invented it in Paris in 1816 and published it in 1819.

claims.text: Physicians listened by pressing an ear to the chest; Laennec, examining a young woman, found this awkward and used a paper tube, which carried the heart sounds clearly.
vo: doctors pressed an ear to the chest. with a young woman patient laennec found that awkward; the tube carried her heartbeat clearly

claims.text: He named the instrument the stethoscope from the Greek stethos (chest) and skopein (to look/examine) and published his treatise in 1819.
vo: he named it the stethoscope, from the greek for chest and look, and published his findings in 1819

claims.text: Laennec died of tuberculosis in 1826 at the age of 45.
vo: laennec died at 45 of tuberculosis, the disease his own instrument diagnosed best
